Page 1 Test Document: Historical Background of the Indian Constitution Purpose: Upload this PDF to your AI Study Platform and generate a source-grounded timeline in Visual Learning Mode. Recommended test input Topic Historical Background of the Indian Constitution Visual type Timeline Language English Grounding rule: The roadmap should use only the milestones and facts stated in this document. If a node cannot be linked to one of the source IDs S1-S6, it should be excluded. Chronological Milestones 1. 1773 - Regulating Act, 1773 Key change The British Parliament began direct regulation of the East India Company. The Governor of Bengal became the Governor-General of Bengal, and an executive council was created. UPSC relevance Marks the beginning of parliamentary control and administrative centralisation in British India. Source ID S1 2. 1784 - Pitt's India Act, 1784 Key change A Board of Control was established to supervise the Company's civil, military and revenue affairs. Commercial functions remained with the Court of Directors. UPSC relevance Introduced dual control: political supervision by the British government and commercial management by the Company. Source ID S1 3. 1813 - Charter Act, 1813 Key change The Company's trade monopoly was largely ended, except in tea and trade with China. The Act also permitted greater missionary and educational activity. UPSC relevance Reduced the Company's commercial exclusivity and widened public activity in India. Source ID S2

Page 2 4. 1833 - Charter Act, 1833 Key change The Governor-General of Bengal became the Governor-General of India. The Company ceased its commercial activities and became a purely administrative body. UPSC relevance A major step toward centralised government and uniform legislation for British India. Source ID S2 5. 1853 - Charter Act, 1853 Key change The legislative and executive functions of the Governor-General's Council were separated more clearly. Open competition for civil service recruitment was introduced in principle. UPSC relevance Important for legislative specialisation and the later development of merit-based civil services. Source ID S2 6. 1858 - Government of India Act, 1858 Key change After the Revolt of 1857, rule was transferred from the East India Company to the British Crown. The office of the Secretary of State for India was created. UPSC relevance Ended Company rule and began direct Crown administration. Source ID S3 7. 1861 - Indian Councils Act, 1861 Key change Indians could be nominated to legislative councils, and legislative powers were restored to Bombay and Madras. The portfolio system gained statutory recognition. UPSC relevance Introduced limited Indian association with lawmaking and encouraged administrative decentralisation. Source ID S3 8. 1909 - Indian Councils Act, 1909 Key change Legislative councils were enlarged and the principle of separate electorates for Muslims was introduced. The reforms are commonly associated with Morley and Minto. UPSC relevance Expanded representation but institutionalised communal electorates. Source ID S4

Page 3 9. 1919 - Government of India Act, 1919 Key change Dyarchy was introduced in the provinces, dividing subjects into reserved and transferred categories. A bicameral central legislature was established. UPSC relevance Advanced limited provincial responsibility and legislative development. Source ID S4 10. 1935 - Government of India Act, 1935 Key change Provincial autonomy was introduced, subjects were divided through federal, provincial and concurrent lists, and a proposed federation was outlined. UPSC relevance Provided several administrative and federal features later adapted in the Constitution of India. Source ID S5 11. 1947 - Indian Independence Act, 1947 Key change British rule ended and India and Pakistan became independent dominions. The Constituent Assembly also functioned as the legislative body of the new Dominion of India. UPSC relevance Provided the legal transition from colonial rule to independent constitutional government. Source ID S5 12. 1946-1950 - Constituent Assembly to Republic Key change The Constituent Assembly first met in December 1946. The Constitution was adopted on 26 November 1949 and came into force on 26 January 1950. UPSC relevance Completed the transition to a sovereign democratic republic under a written Constitution. Source ID S6

11. 1947 - Indian Independence Act, 1947 Key change British rule ended and India and Pakistan became independent dominions. The Constituent Assembly also functioned as the legislative body of the new Dominion of India. UPSC relevance Provided the legal transition from colonial rule to independent constitutional government. Source ID S5 12. 1946-1950 - Constituent Assembly to Republic Key change The Constituent Assembly first met in December 1946. The Constitution was adopted on 26 November 1949 and came into force on 26 January 1950. UPSC relevance Completed the transition to a sovereign democratic republic under a written Constitution. Source ID S6

Page 4 Source Notes for RAG Validation S1 Early parliamentary control: Regulating Act, 1773 and Pitt's India Act, 1784. S2 Charter Acts and centralisation: 1813, 1833 and 1853. S3 Transfer to Crown rule and limited legislative participation: 1858 and 1861. S4 Representative reforms and provincial responsibility: 1909 and 1919. S5 Late colonial constitutional framework and independence: 1935 and 1947. S6 Constituent Assembly, adoption of the Constitution, and commencement of the Republic. Expected Manual Validation - The generated timeline contains no more than 12 nodes. - Every year and Act in the SVG matches this document. - Each roadmap node is linked internally to one or more source IDs. - No extra Act, year or constitutional fact is invented. - Node labels do not overlap at normal zoom. - Zoom, fit-to-screen and pan work in the roadmap viewer. - SVG download opens correctly in a browser. - Save and delete actions update roadmap history. - A topic not supported by the indexed PDF returns an insufficient-context message. - Browser console contains no new error caused by roadmap generation. Suggested negative test Ask for a roadmap on "Quantum Computing Hardware Architecture" while only this PDF is indexed. The system should refuse or return insufficient context instead of inventing a roadmap. Note: This PDF is a purpose-built test document for local RAG and visual-roadmap validation. The wording is original and deliberately concise.
